q1_issues.issue: 'not always accompanied' is rendered as a blanket strength-0.0 denial, which asserts that fame is NEVER accompanied by success — a strictly stronger and different claim than that it is not accompanied on every occasion.

The bare abstract mass subject 'fame' is given an existential witness sk_fame_1 (positing one specific instance of fame) while the equally bare 'success' is kept as a constant; a bare mass noun stays a constant/kind.
Both arguments are bare kind-denoting mass NPs, which is the relational-generic trigger, so the licensed form is the opaque kind-level relation rather than a per-instance event bundle.
No QuantifierPhrase companion records the frequency word, so this parse is indistinguishable from a plain unquantified denial.

q2_gaps: negated frequency adverb ('not always' / 'not usually') — the frequency-adverb map assigns strengths only to positive adverbs plus 'never', and the 'not all / not every' counterexample-witness pattern is defined over entities, not over occasions
notes: The passive role mapping (by-phrase to Agent even though inanimate and stative, object to Theme) does follow the instruction set. The defect is quantificational force: the emitted atom claims far more than the sentence does.
